newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CORPORATE BONDS -- New junk higher as usual.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CORPORATE BONDS -- New junk higher as usual.

text.p: High-yield corporate debt issuance continued to reap the benefits of positive mutual fund cash flow on Wednesday, while secondary prices were mostly flat amid Treasury and stock weakness, dealers said.

Investment-grade activity was also focused on fresh supply as issuers commenced capital-raising efforts ahead of a possible interest rate hike at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in July.
Spreads were steady as U.S. Treasury prices dipped following a report of a narrower-than-expected trade gap and heavy long-end selling, traders said.

Issuers aiming to capture a "window of opportunity" placed two deals on Wednesday totaling $600 million. The bulk of new issuance, however, is not expected until after the U.S. Memorial Day holiday weekend, however, syndicates said.
Associates Corp first tapped the market with $300 million 6.70 percent Aa3/AA-minus rated four-year notes, priced to yield 6.749 percent via lead manager J.P. Morgan Securities.

Also, cellular, local and long-distance provider Frontier Corp issued $300 million in 7.25 percent A3/single-A rated seven-year notes to yield 7.527 percent, or 58 basis points over the Treasury curve via a Salomon Brothers syndicate.

The performance of new high-yielding issues, even in the face of weakness in adjacent markets, captured the market's attention. Cash flows were universally cited as the driving force, and buyside sources suggest flows will be solidly on the plus side when reported later this week.

"We're seeing cash come in, I think the whole universe is seeing cash come in," said Thomas Ole Dial, executive vice president and chief investment officer at The Northstar Funds. "There were negligible defaults last year, and as long as you have an economy doing what it's doing, I can't imagine a scenario that could be better for the high-yield market."

Reflecting the positive environment, Argentina's Compania Latinoamericano Infraestructura Servicios SA (CLISA)'s $100 million seven-year BB-minus 11-5/8 percent senior guaranteed note issue was seen trading in a 102 bid, 102-1/2 offer market near the close compared with a par pricing.

The issue, priced via Citicorp Securities, was well oversubscribed and placed with 60 percent traditional high-yield accounts and 40 percent emerging market accounts, according to a source close to the deal.
Also, a $105 million issue from Wells Aluminum Corp priced as 10-1/8s at par traded up more than one point on Thursday, according to buyside sources.

The reemergence of some telecom issues from the postponed list this week may not get the same hearty reception as industrial credits, fund managers said. But they shied away from making a sweeping statement about the sector with some well-known names like Brooks Fiber Properties and InterCel Inc planning debt offerings.
"People are still looking for new deals, but it's got to be quality paper," one trader said.

Secondary high-yield prices were unchanged "but not firm" as the Treasury market weakened, traders said. Treasuries were plagued by hedge fund selling in the long end as well as the narrowing trade deficit, analysts said.
The 10-year Treasury note fell 12/32 to yield 6.73 percent and the 30-year bond was off 23/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
